context:
Follow existing interactive prompt patterns in benchbox/cli/benchmarks.py
(`prompt_data_format`, `prompt_output_location`) to add `prompt_table_mode`
with a simple numbered choice and normalized return value.

In benchbox/cli/commands/run.py, wire prompt invocation only in interactive
wizard flow and only when table mode was not explicitly supplied on the CLI.
Keep explicit user flags authoritative by checking Click parameter source
before applying wizard-selected value.

In benchbox/cli/dryrun.py, extend `generate_cli_command` and
`display_interactive_preview` so the generated command always includes
`--table-mode` for reproducibility, and preview table shows a "Table Mode"
row.

In benchbox/cli/preferences.py and run quick-restart save/load callsites,
persist `table_mode` and surface a concise mode hint in quick restart summary
for non-default mode to avoid hidden configuration reuse.
description:
Interactive benchmark setup currently does not explicitly surface table mode
(`native` vs `external`) even though `--table-mode` exists in CLI options.
This creates ambiguity in wizard-driven runs and in the generated
"Equivalent CLI command" preview.

This TODO adds table mode to interactive UX and command rendering so users can:
1) select or confirm table mode in wizard flow,
2) see selected mode in preview output, and
3) copy an equivalent command that includes `--table-mode`.

The implementation must preserve existing non-interactive semantics and keep
explicit CLI flags authoritative when provided.

anti_patterns.dont: leak interactive-only prompt behavior into --non-interactive paths
anti_patterns.instead: keep prompt logic gated by TTY interactive flow
anti_patterns.why: CI workflows rely on deterministic flag-only behavior

anti_patterns.dont: override a user-provided --table-mode with interactive prompt output
anti_patterns.instead: skip prompting when table_mode came from CLI
